parsed_output.analysis: The model captures the overall hierarchy DoorsClosing -> InMotion with Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching substates and the Arrived transition to Stopping, but several behavioral details required by the specification are missing or inverted. Entry actions for Accelerating, the obstacle detection / EmergencyStopping signal handling, and the sending behavior of the Approaching substate are not represented as specified, and an undocumented return from EmergencyStopping to InMotion is present.

issues.issue: Missing Entry/Accelerate action on Accelerating substate entry
issues.reason: Specification 8 requires the system to enter the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the Entry/Accelerate action. The model shows [*] --> Accelerating with no entry action, so the required Accelerate action on entry to Accelerating is absent.
issues.where: state InMotion { [*] --> Accelerating } and Accelerating definition

issues.issue: Obstacle Detected signal used as trigger instead of effect on entry to EmergencyStopping
issues.reason: Specification 2-3 states that when an obstacle is detected the system enters EmergencyStopping, which includes the action Emergency Stop and sends the Obstacle Detected signal. The model uses Obstacle Detected as the transition trigger into EmergencyStopping and does not show Emergency Stop as an entry action and sending Obstacle Detected on entry.
issues.where: InMotion --> EmergencyStopping: Obstacle Detected and EmergencyStopping state

issues.issue: Obstacle Detected signal sent on exit from EmergencyStopping and spurious return to InMotion
issues.reason: Specification 3 requires the Obstacle Detected signal to be sent on entry to EmergencyStopping, not on exit, and the specification does not define a return transition from EmergencyStopping to InMotion. The model sends Obstacle Detected on exit and creates an undocumented return to InMotion.

issues.issue: Approaching substate Send signal placed on an exit transition to the parent instead of while in the substate
issues.reason: Specification 9 requires the Approaching substate to send the Send signal and continue to approach the destination while remaining in the substate. The model models Send as an exit action on a transition from Approaching back to InMotion, which is not specified.

Specification 10 requires the system to remain in Approaching while nearing the destination until it is ready to stop or decelerate. The model provides an unconditional exit from Approaching to InMotion with only an exit/Send label, with no stop/decelerate condition and no transition to Stopping from Approaching.

issues.issue: Stopping state is referenced but never defined
issues.reason: Specification 2 references a Stopping state reached from InMotion on arrival. The model contains a transition to Stopping but no Stopping state definition, so the target state is undefined in the model.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1. The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal. 
2. In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected. 
3. When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal. 
4. Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion. 
5. The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal. 
6. If the system is in the Accelerating substate and approaches its destination, it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal. 
7. The system in the Cruising substate transitions to the Approaching substate when it approaches the destination, triggered by the "Approached/Decelerate" signal. 
8. The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action. 
9. In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination. 
10. The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> DoorsClosing
DoorsClosing: Doors are closing
DoorsClosing --> InMotion: Closed/SendDeparted
state InMotion {
[*] --> Accelerating
Accelerating: Accelerating
Accelerating --> Cruising: Reached Cruising/Cruise
Accelerating --> Approaching: Approached/Decelerate

Cruising: Cruising
Cruising --> Approaching: Approached/Decelerate
Approaching: Approaching
Approaching --> InMotion:exit/Send
}
InMotion --> Stopping: Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived
InMotion --> EmergencyStopping: Obstacle Detected
EmergencyStopping: Emergency Stop
EmergencyStopping --> InMotion:exit/Send Obstacle Detected
@enduml
